```ts
    const a = b2t4Write(root, B2T4_A);
    const b = b2t4Write(root, B2T4_B);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.loadHandcheckPlan(b2t4Flags([{ ...a, sha: B2T4_OTHER }, b]), b2t4Fin())))
      .toEqual({ word: 'input-sha-mismatch', detail: `judged: expected ${B2T4_OTHER}, measured ${a.sha}` });
  });

  const w = b2t4Write;
  it.each([
    ['a file of another kind', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { kind: 'ccrc-history-w2-other' } }), w(r, B2T4_B)], () => 'judged 1 is not a judged file'],
    ['the pilot section', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A), w(r, B2T4_B, { over: { section: 'pilot' } })], () => 'judged 2 section "pilot", wanted quiz'],
    ['another record', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A), w(r, B2T4_B, { over: { record_sha256: B2T4_OTHER } })],
      () => `judged 2 record "${B2T4_OTHER}", not this record's ${B2T4_RECORD_SHA}: run judge on that node under this record`],
    ['another frozen list', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { frozen_sha256: B2T4_OTHER } }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      () => `judged 1 frozen "${B2T4_OTHER}", not this record's ${B2T4_FROZEN_SHA}`],
    ['another judge map', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { map_sha256: B2T4_OTHER } }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      () => `judged 1 map "${B2T4_OTHER}", not this record's judge map ${b2t4MapSha(b2t4Fin())}`],
    ['a store that is no node', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { store_id: B2T4_NOWHERE } }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      () => `judged 1 store "${B2T4_NOWHERE}" is not one of the record's nodes`],
    ['one node twice', (r: string) => { const a = w(r, B2T4_A); return [a, a, w(r, B2T4_B)]; }, () => `judged 2 store ${B2T4_A} repeats judged 1`],
    ['another judge model', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { judge_model: 'claude-opus-9-2' } }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      () => `judged 1 judge ${JSON.stringify(['claude-opus-9-2', 'v1', B2T4_RUBRIC_SHA])} is not the record's ${JSON.stringify([W6_MODEL, 'v1', B2T4_RUBRIC_SHA])}`],
    ['another reply cap', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { reply_max_bytes: 1024 } }), w(r, B2T4_B)], () => 'judged 1 reply_max_bytes 1024, not 16384'],
    ['stamps that are not words', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A, { over: { stamps: [1] } }), w(r, B2T4_B)], () => 'judged 1 stamps is not a list of words'],
    ['an item that is no judge id', (r: string) => {
      const a = w(r, B2T4_A);
      return [b2t4Save(a.dir, { ...a.doc, items: [...a.doc.items, { id: 'k0001', outcome: 'judged', label: 'uncertain', attempts: [] }] }), w(r, B2T4_B)];
    }, () => 'judged 1 item "k0001" is not a judge id'],
    ['an item outside the map', (r: string) => {
      const a = w(r, B2T4_A);
      return [b2t4Save(a.dir, { ...a.doc, items: [...a.doc.items, { id: 'j0099', outcome: 'judged', label: 'uncertain', attempts: [] }] }), w(r, B2T4_B)];
    }, () => 'judged 1 item j0099 is not in the judge map'],
    ['an item two files carry', (r: string) => {
      const a = w(r, B2T4_A);
      const b = w(r, B2T4_B);
      return [a, b2t4Save(b.dir, { ...b.doc, items: [...b.doc.items, a.doc.items[0]] })];
    }, (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 2 item ${ws[0]!.doc.items[0].id as string} repeats`],
    ['an item of another node', (r: string) => {
      const a = w(r, B2T4_A);
      const b = w(r, B2T4_B);
      return [b2t4Save(a.dir, { ...a.doc, items: [...a.doc.items, b.doc.items[0]] }), b];
    }, (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 1 item ${ws[1]!.doc.items[0].id as string} names a question of another node`],
    ['an outcome outside the two', (r: string) => [b2t4Patch(w(r, B2T4_A), (i) => i.outcome === 'judged', { outcome: 'skipped' }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 1 item ${b2t4IdWhere(ws[0]!, (i) => i.outcome === 'skipped')} outcome "skipped"`],
    ['a judged item with no label', (r: string) => [b2t4Patch(w(r, B2T4_A), (i) => i.outcome === 'judged', { label: null }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 1 item ${b2t4IdWhere(ws[0]!, (i) => i.outcome === 'judged' && i.label === null)} judged with label null`],
    ['a judge-failed item with a label', (r: string) => [b2t4Patch(w(r, B2T4_A), (i) => i.outcome === 'judge-failed', { label: 'uncertain' }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 1 item ${b2t4IdWhere(ws[0]!, (i) => i.outcome === 'judge-failed')} judge-failed with label "uncertain"`],
    ['a judged item labelled correct', (r: string) => [b2t4Patch(w(r, B2T4_A), (i) => i.outcome === 'judged', { label: 'correct' }), w(r, B2T4_B)],
      (ws: B2t4Write[]) => `judged 1 item ${b2t4IdWhere(ws[0]!, (i) => i.label === 'correct')} judged with label "correct"`],
    ['a node holding questions with no judged file', (r: string) => [w(r, B2T4_A)],
      () => `judged-missing 1 node(s) (first ${B2T4_B}): pass every node's judged.json that holds frozen questions`],
  ] as Array<[string, (root: string) => B2t4Write[], (ws: B2t4Write[]) => string]>)('%s refuses input-invalid, naming the file by its position', (_name, setup, detail) => {
    const ws = setup(mkTmp('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-refuse-'));
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.loadHandcheckPlan(b2t4Flags(ws), b2t4Fin()))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: detail(ws) });
  });
});

describe('W2-5b2 Task 4: the sheet is blinded and shows each item as the judge saw it (W2-D81, W2-D54)', () => {
  it('the sheet is a header, the signed rubric as comments, then one block per item: its kind, question, F, answer field and reply', () => {
    const e = B2T4_ENTRIES[0]!;
    const input = W5B5.judgeInputOf(e, 'Two lines here.\nANSWER: npm run b2t4-other', W6_IDX);
    const text = B2T4.handcheckSheetText({ recordSha256: B2T4_RECORD_SHA, frozenSha256: B2T4_FROZEN_SHA, rubricId: 'v1', items: [{ id: 'j0003', input }] });
    expect(text).toBe([
      '# ccrc history W2 hand-check sheet (W2-D81): one block per item, in id order.',
      `# record ${B2T4_RECORD_SHA}`,
      `# frozen ${B2T4_FROZEN_SHA}`,
      '# items 1',
      '# Label every item in a separate file, one line per item: "<id> uncertain" or "<id> fabricated".',
      '# A line that starts with "#" is a comment. Neither the arm nor the judge\'s label is shown here.',
      '# The rubric the judge was given (v1):',
      ...(w5b5Gate.RUBRICS as Record<string, string>)['v1']!.split('\n').map((l) => `#   ${l}`),
      '',
      '== j0003 ==',
      'kind: command',
      'question:',
      `| ${e.question}`,
      'expected:',
      `| ${e.fact}`,
      'answer field:',
      '| npm run b2t4-other',
      'reply:',
      '| Two lines here.',
      '| ANSWER: npm run b2t4-other',
      '',
    ].join('\n'));
    expect(() => B2T4.handcheckSheetText({ recordSha256: B2T4_RECORD_SHA, frozenSha256: B2T4_FROZEN_SHA, rubricId: 'v2', items: [] })).toThrow(TypeError);
  });

  it('every field line is quoted with "| ", an empty line as "|", so no reply line can open a block; no answer field reads (none)', () => {
    const e = B2T4_ENTRIES[1]!;
    const input = W5B5.judgeInputOf(e, 'first\n\n== j0004 ==\nkind: sha', W6_IDX);
    expect(input.answer_field).toBeNull();
    const text = B2T4.handcheckSheetText({ recordSha256: B2T4_RECORD_SHA, frozenSha256: B2T4_FROZEN_SHA, rubricId: 'v1', items: [{ id: 'j0003', input }] });
    expect(text.slice(text.indexOf('\n== j0003 ==\n') + 1)).toBe(['== j0003 ==', 'kind: command', 'question:', `| ${e.question}`, 'expected:', `| ${e.fact}`,
      'answer field: (none)', 'reply:', '| first', '|', '| == j0004 ==', '| kind: sha', ''].join('\n'));
    expect(text.split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('== '))).toEqual(['== j0003 ==']);
  });

  it('blinded: the sheet\'s bytes do not move when every judge label flips or items swap between judged and judge-failed, and it names no arm', () => {
    const fin = b2t4Fin({ share: 1 });
    const one = b2t4Both('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-blind-a-', fin);
    const swapped: B2t4Outcome = (e, a) => {
      const o = b2t4Outcome(e, a);
      if (o === null) return null;
      if (o.outcome === 'judge-failed') return { outcome: 'judged', label: 'fabricated' };
      if (e === 2 && a === 0) return { outcome: 'judge-failed', label: null };
      return { outcome: 'judged', label: o.label === 'fabricated' ? 'uncertain' : 'fabricated' };
    };
    const two = b2t4Both('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-blind-b-', fin, { outcome: swapped });
    expect(two.plan.items.map((i) => [i.outcome, i.judge])).not.toEqual(one.plan.items.map((i) => [i.outcome, i.judge]));
    expect(two.plan.sampled).toEqual(one.plan.sampled);
    const sheet = B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, one.plan).sheetText;
    expect(B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, two.plan).sheetText).toBe(sheet);
    for (const arm of W5B5_ARMS) expect(sheet, arm).not.toMatch(new RegExp(`\\b${arm}\\b`));
    expect(sheet.split('\n').filter((l) => /^(\| )?LABEL:/.test(l)), 'no judge reply line').toEqual([]);
    expect(sheet.split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('== ')), 'one block per sheet id').toEqual(one.plan.sampled.map((id) => `== ${id} ==`));
    const man = JSON.parse(B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, one.plan).manifestText) as Record<string, any>;
    expect(Object.keys(man.items[0]).sort()).toEqual(['id', 'input_sha256']);
    for (const arm of W5B5_ARMS) expect(JSON.stringify(man), `manifest: ${arm}`).not.toMatch(new RegExp(`\\b${arm}\\b`));
  });

  it('judgeInputFault holds an input to its six keys, v 1, its strings, the entry\'s kind, the 16 KiB cap and its canonical bytes', () => {
    const e = B2T4_ENTRIES[0]!;
    const good = W5B5.judgeInputOf(e, b2t4Reply(0, 0), W6_IDX) as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
    const bytesOf = (v: unknown): Buffer => Buffer.from(`${w5b5Lib.canonicalJson(v) as string}\n`, 'utf8');
    const fault = (v: Record<string, unknown>, bytes: Buffer = bytesOf(v)): string | null => B2T4.judgeInputFault(v, e, bytes);
    const max = B2T4.JUDGE_REPLY_MAX_BYTES;
    expect(fault(good)).toBeNull();
    expect(fault({ ...good, arm: 'x' }), 'a seventh key').toBe('keys');
    expect(fault(Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(good).filter(([k]) => k !== 'reply'))), 'no reply').toBe('keys');
    expect(fault({ ...good, v: 2 })).toBe('version');
    expect(fault({ ...good, reply: 7 })).toBe('field-type');
    expect(fault({ ...good, answer_field: 7 })).toBe('field-type');
    expect(fault({ ...good, kind: 'sha' })).toBe('kind');
    expect(fault({ ...good, reply: 'x'.repeat(max + 1) })).toBe('over-cap');
    expect(fault({ ...good, answer_field: 'x'.repeat(max + 1) })).toBe('over-cap');
    expect(fault({ ...good, reply: 'x'.repeat(max) }), 'CONTROL: at the cap').toBeNull();
    expect(fault(good, Buffer.from(`${JSON.stringify(good, null, 1)}\n`)), 'indented').toBe('not-canonical');
    const raw = bytesOf(good);
    expect(fault(good, raw.subarray(0, raw.length - 1)), 'no final newline').toBe('not-canonical');
    const at = raw.indexOf(Buffer.from('I think'));
    const bad = Buffer.concat([raw.subarray(0, at), Buffer.from([0xff]), raw.subarray(at + 1)]);
    expect(fault(JSON.parse(bad.toString('utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>, bad), 'an invalid UTF-8 byte').toBe('not-canonical');
  });

  it('each sampled item\'s input is read as judge left it: a missing file, a link or another kind refuses input-invalid, naming its node and path', () => {
    const fin = b2t4Fin({ share: 1 });
    const x = b2t4Both('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-inputs-', fin);
    const [i0, i1] = (x.a.doc.items as Array<Record<string, any>>).map((i) => i.id as string);
    expect(B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, x.plan).sheetText, 'CONTROL').toContain(`\n== ${i0!} ==\n`);
    const p0 = join(x.a.dir, 'judge', `${i0!}.input.json`);
    const keep = readFileSync(p0);
    const where = `judged ${B2T4_A} judge/${i0!}.input.json`;
    rmSync(p0);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, x.plan))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: `${where} unreadable ENOENT` });
    symlinkSync(join(x.a.dir, 'judge', `${i1!}.input.json`), p0);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, x.plan))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: `${where} not-regular` });
    rmSync(p0);
    writeFileSync(p0, `${w5b5Lib.canonicalJson({ ...(JSON.parse(keep.toString('utf8')) as Record<string, unknown>), kind: 'sha' }) as string}\n`);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.handcheckSheetOf(fin, x.plan))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: `${where} kind` });
  });
});

describe('W2-5b2 Task 4: the label reader is strict (Q19)', () => {
  it('comments, blank lines, and spaces or tabs between an id and its word are read; each sheet id answers its word, in file order', () => {
    const { plan } = b2t4Ready();
    expect(plan.sampled).toHaveLength(6);
    const [x, y, ...rest] = plan.sampled;
    const tab = String.fromCharCode(9);
    const text = b2t4Text(['# the operator\'s labels', '', `${x!}${tab}uncertain`, `${y!}   fabricated ${tab}`, '#', ...rest.map((id) => `${id} fabricated`)]);
    expect([...B2T4.parseHandcheckLabels(text, plan).entries()]).toEqual([[x, 'uncertain'], [y, 'fabricated'], ...rest.map((id) => [id, 'fabricated'])]);
    expect(B2T4.HANDCHECK_LABELS).toEqual(['uncertain', 'fabricated']);
  });

  it.each([
    ['an id alone', (l: string[]) => [l[0]!.split(' ')[0]!, ...l.slice(1)], () => B2T4_MALFORMED(1)],
    ['a space before the id', (l: string[]) => [` ${l[0]!}`, ...l.slice(1)], () => B2T4_MALFORMED(1)],
    ['a comment after the word', (l: string[]) => [`${l[0]!} # sure`, ...l.slice(1)], () => B2T4_MALFORMED(1)],
    ['a carriage return after the word', (l: string[]) => [`${l[0]!}${String.fromCharCode(13)}`, ...l.slice(1)], () => B2T4_MALFORMED(1)],
    ['an id that is no judge id', (l: string[]) => ['x0001 uncertain', ...l], () => B2T4_MALFORMED(1)],
    ['the word correct', (l: string[]) => [`${l[0]!.split(' ')[0]!} correct`, ...l.slice(1)], () => 'labels line 1 label "correct" is not one of uncertain, fabricated'],
    ['a capitalised word', (l: string[]) => [`${l[0]!.split(' ')[0]!} Uncertain`, ...l.slice(1)], () => 'labels line 1 label "Uncertain" is not one of uncertain, fabricated'],
    ['an id not on the sheet', (l: string[], x: B2t4Ready) => [...l, `${x.notDrawn} uncertain`],
      (x: B2t4Ready) => `labels line ${x.plan.sampled.length + 1} id ${x.notDrawn} is not on the sheet`],
    ['an id twice', (l: string[]) => [...l, l[0]!], (x: B2t4Ready) => `labels line ${x.plan.sampled.length + 1} repeats ${x.plan.sampled[0]!}`],
    ['a sampled judged id with no line', (l: string[], x: B2t4Ready) => l.filter((s) => s.split(' ')[0] !== x.plan.required[0]),
      (x: B2t4Ready) => `labels-missing 1 sampled id(s) (first ${x.plan.required[0]!}): label every sampled item`],
  ] as Array<[string, (l: string[], x: B2t4Ready) => string[], (x: B2t4Ready) => string]>)('%s refuses input-invalid', (_name, edit, detail) => {
    const x = b2t4Ready();
    expect(B2T4.parseHandcheckLabels(b2t4Text(b2t4Agree(x.plan)), x.plan).size, 'CONTROL: the unedited file reads').toBe(x.plan.sampled.length);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.parseHandcheckLabels(b2t4Text(edit(b2t4Agree(x.plan), x)), x.plan))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: detail(x) });
  });

  it('a judge-failed id left unlabelled is read: its label stays null, it is named unlabelled, and the gate\'s verdict waits (incomplete)', () => {
    const { plan, failed } = b2t4Ready();
    expect(failed).toHaveLength(2);
    const labels = B2T4.parseHandcheckLabels(b2t4Text(b2t4Agree(plan).filter((l) => !failed.includes(l.split(' ')[0]!))), plan);
    expect(labels.size).toBe(plan.required.length);
    const res = B2T4.handcheckResultOf(plan, labels);
    expect(res.unlabelled).toEqual(failed);
    for (const id of failed) expect(res.items.find((i) => i.id === id), id).toMatchObject({ label: null, judgeFailed: true, operator: null });
    const verdict = (rs: B2t4Result): string => (w5b5Gate.decideGate(b2t4GateInputs(rs) as never) as { verdict: string }).verdict;
    expect(verdict(res)).toBe('incomplete');
    const all = B2T4.handcheckResultOf(plan, B2T4.parseHandcheckLabels(b2t4Text(b2t4Agree(plan)), plan));
    expect(all.unlabelled).toEqual([]);
    expect(verdict(all), 'CONTROL: every judge-failed item labelled').not.toBe('incomplete');
  });

  it('readHandcheckLabels checks the file\'s sha before a byte is read, and refuses bytes that are not UTF-8', () => {
    const { plan } = b2t4Ready();
    const dir = mkTmp('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-labels-file-');
    const text = b2t4Text(b2t4Agree(plan));
    const p = join(dir, 'labels.txt');
    writeFileSync(p, text, { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(B2T4.readHandcheckLabels(p, sha256Hex(text), plan).size, 'CONTROL').toBe(plan.sampled.length);
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.readHandcheckLabels(p, B2T4_OTHER, plan)))
      .toEqual({ word: 'input-sha-mismatch', detail: `labels: expected ${B2T4_OTHER}, measured ${sha256Hex(text)}` });
    const bad = Buffer.concat([Buffer.from('# the operator\'s labels '), Buffer.from([0xff]), Buffer.from(`\n${text}`)]);
    const q = join(dir, 'labels-bad.txt');
    writeFileSync(q, bad, { mode: 0o600 });
    expect(b2t4Refusal(() => B2T4.readHandcheckLabels(q, sha256Hex(bad), plan))).toEqual({ word: 'input-invalid', detail: 'labels not-utf8' });
  });
});

describe('W2-5b2 Task 4: the operator\'s label replaces the judge\'s, and agreement is by arm (W2-D81)', () => {
  it('sampled items take the operator\'s word, the rest keep the judge\'s, a labelled judge-failed item is no pair, and agreement is the gate\'s per arm', () => {
    const { plan } = b2t4Both('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-override-');
    const byId = new Map(plan.items.map((i) => [i.id, i]));
    const flip = (l: string | null): string => (l === 'fabricated' ? 'uncertain' : 'fabricated');
    const flipped = W5B5_ARMS.map((arm) => plan.required.find((id) => byId.get(id)!.arm === arm)!);
    const operator = new Map(plan.sampled.map((id): [string, string] => {
      const i = byId.get(id)!;
      return [id, i.outcome === 'judge-failed' ? 'fabricated' : flipped.includes(id) ? flip(i.judge) : i.judge!];
    }));
    const res = B2T4.handcheckResultOf(plan, operator);
    expect(res.items.map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(plan.items.map((i) => i.id));
    for (const r of res.items) {
      const i = byId.get(r.id)!;
      expect(r, r.id).toEqual({ id: i.id, qid: i.qid, arm: i.arm, label: operator.get(r.id) ?? i.judge, judgeFailed: i.outcome === 'judge-failed',
        operator: operator.get(r.id) ?? null });
    }
    const pairs = plan.required.map((id) => ({ arm: byId.get(id)!.arm, judge: byId.get(id)!.judge, operator: operator.get(id) }));
    expect(res.agreement).toEqual(w5b5Gate.handcheckAgreement(pairs as never));
    for (const arm of W5B5_ARMS) expect(res.agreement[arm], `${arm}: one of its two sampled items agrees`).toEqual(w5b5Gate.frac(1, 2));
    expect(res.unlabelled).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('an operator label for an id that is not on the sheet is a defect the reader never lets through: TypeError', () => {
    const x = b2t4Ready();
    expect(() => B2T4.handcheckResultOf(x.plan, new Map([[x.notDrawn, 'uncertain']]))).toThrow(TypeError);
    expect(() => B2T4.handcheckResultOf(x.plan, new Map(x.plan.sampled.map((id): [string, string] => [id, 'uncertain']))), 'CONTROL: the sheet\'s own ids').not.toThrow();
  });
});

describe('W2-5b2 Task 4: handcheck --sheet (W2-D81, W2-D24; Q2, Q23)', () => {
  /** Flags that pass `handcheck --sheet`'s grammar; the record inputs are placeholders the injected loader never reads. */
  function b2t4SheetFlags(out: string, ws: B2t4Write[], extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Record<string, unknown> {
    const sha = 'a'.repeat(64);
    const input = '/home/u/fixture-input.json';
    return { sheet: true, out, record: input, 'record-sha256': sha, part1: input, 'part1-sha256': sha, frozen: input, 'frozen-sha256': sha, ...b2t4Flags(ws), ...extra };
  }
  const b2t4Deps = (fin: B2t4Fin): Record<string, unknown> => ({ loadFinal: () => fin, now: () => Date.now() });
  const B2T4_MOVED = (): Record<string, string> => ({ ...w5b4Shas(), 'deploy/measure-history.py': w5b4Hex('moved') });
  /** `handcheck --sheet` over W2-5b1 Task 4's quiz fixture, with the judged files given. */
  const b2t4Argv = (fx: { out: string; f: W5b4Saved; d: W5b4Saved; fz: W5b4Saved }, judged: string[], shas: string[], extra: string[] = []): string[] =>
    ['handcheck', '--sheet', '--out', fx.out, ...w5b4Inp('record', fx.f), ...w5b4Inp('part1', fx.d), ...w5b4Inp('frozen', fx.fz),
      ...judged.flatMap((p, i) => ['--judged', p, '--judged-sha256', shas[i]!]), ...extra];

  it('handcheck takes --sheet and only its form\'s flags', () => {
    const home = mkTmp('ccrc-w2-5b2-t4-grammar-');
    const out = join(home, 'report-out');
    const sha = 'a'.repeat(64);
    const said = (argv: string[]): [unknown, string] => { const r = runDriver(home, argv); return [r.code, r.stderr]; };
    expect(said(['handcheck', '--out', out])).toEqual([2, refusalLine('args-invalid', 'handcheck wants --sheet')]);
```

(c) Replace `loadInput`'s definition, which at 92dac5764 reads exactly

```js
export function loadInput(label, p, sha256, words = INPUT_WORDS, cap = OUT_JSON_CAP) {
  if (typeof sha256 !== 'string' || !SHA256_RE.test(sha256)) refuse('args-invalid', `--${label}-sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex`);
  if (typeof p !== 'string' || p === '') refuse('args-invalid', `--${label} names no path`);
  const abs = path.resolve(p);
  const g = insideGitTree(path.dirname(abs));
  if (g.state === 'inside') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} in-git-tree ${g.at}`);
  if (g.state === 'unmeasured') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} git-unmeasured ${g.at} ${g.code}`);
  const read = readPlain(abs, cap);
  if (read.state === 'absent') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} unreadable ENOENT`);
  if (read.state === 'bad') refuse(words.invalid, read.why === 'unreadable' ? `${label} unreadable ${read.code}` : `${label} ${read.why}`);
  const got = sha256Hex(read.bytes);
  if (got !== sha256) refuse(words.sha, `${label}: expected ${sha256}, measured ${got}`);
  let value;
  try {
    value = JSON.parse(read.bytes.toString('utf8'));
  } catch {
    refuse(words.invalid, `${label} not-json`);
  }
  return { path: abs, sha256: got, value };
}
```

with the following (the doc comment above it stays as it is, above `loadInput`; the read moves into `loadInputBytes`, inserted directly above that comment, word for word):

```js
/** One input's bytes, as loadInput reads them: outside any git tree, read whole through readPlain, the bytes' sha256 checked
 *  BEFORE anything reads them (W2-D25, W2-D59). Factored out of loadInput unchanged (W2-5b2 Task 4), so the hand-check's
 *  label file, which is not JSON, is read by the same rule (W2-D12).
 *  @param {string} label  @param {string} p  @param {string} sha256
 *  @returns {{path: string, sha256: string, bytes: Buffer}} */
function loadInputBytes(label, p, sha256, words = INPUT_WORDS, cap = OUT_JSON_CAP) {
  if (typeof sha256 !== 'string' || !SHA256_RE.test(sha256)) refuse('args-invalid', `--${label}-sha256 is not 64 lowercase hex`);
  if (typeof p !== 'string' || p === '') refuse('args-invalid', `--${label} names no path`);
  const abs = path.resolve(p);
  const g = insideGitTree(path.dirname(abs));
  if (g.state === 'inside') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} in-git-tree ${g.at}`);
  if (g.state === 'unmeasured') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} git-unmeasured ${g.at} ${g.code}`);
  const read = readPlain(abs, cap);
  if (read.state === 'absent') refuse(words.invalid, `${label} unreadable ENOENT`);
  if (read.state === 'bad') refuse(words.invalid, read.why === 'unreadable' ? `${label} unreadable ${read.code}` : `${label} ${read.why}`);
  const got = sha256Hex(read.bytes);
  if (got !== sha256) refuse(words.sha, `${label}: expected ${sha256}, measured ${got}`);
  return { path: abs, sha256: got, bytes: read.bytes };
}
```

(e) Directly above the comment line `// The entry guard stays the LAST block of this file`, after the previous W2-5b2 task's section, insert:

```js
// ── W2-5b2 Task 4: the hand-check sheet and the label reader (W2-D81, W2-D54; Q2, Q18, Q19, Q23) ───────────────────
// On the reporting node, over every node's quiz/judged.json gathered into it (act 24), each passed with its sha (Q2):
// the part 2 record first (W2-D24's re-check, through loadFinalRecord), then the judge map recomputed from the record's
// seed and frozen list (W2-5b1 Task 5's judgeMapOf and judgeMapText, the bytes every node pinned), and each judged file
// held to this record, this frozen list, this map, this judge and one named node, its items to that node's questions
// (Q18, R18). The sample is the gate's handcheckSample at the record's share over every judged item, its arm read from
// the map, then every judge-failed item (W2-D81). The sheet shows each sampled item's judge input (masked at its node
// before the judge saw it, the reply and the answer field cut at the judge's cap: W2-D54, D-6470) under its positional
// id, with no arm and no judge label; the manifest beside it names each input by sha. The label reader (Q19) takes
// `<id> uncertain|fabricated` lines and `#` comments, each sheet id at most once and every sampled judged id exactly
// once; a judge-failed id left unlabelled is not refused: its label stays null and decideGate holds the verdict at
// incomplete. The override and agreement are the gate's applyHandcheck and handcheckAgreement (W2-D81). This file never
// spells an arm word: every arm comes from the map, RECALL_ARMS' values (W2-D42).

/** Under the reporting node's --out: the sheet the operator labels, and the manifest naming its inputs. */
export const HANDCHECK_DIR = 'handcheck';
export const HANDCHECK_SHEET_FILE = 'sheet.txt';
export const HANDCHECK_MANIFEST_FILE = 'sheet.json';
export const HANDCHECK_SHEET_KIND = 'ccrc-history-w2-handcheck-sheet';
/** The hand-check is the quiz's (W2-D81); the pilot has none. */
export const HANDCHECK_SECTION = 'quiz';
/** The two words an operator may write (W2-D79's labels); `correct` is the string match's alone (W2-D63). */
export const HANDCHECK_LABELS = Object.freeze(LABELS.filter((l) => l !== 'correct'));
/** One label line (Q19): an id, spaces or tabs, one word, and nothing after but spaces or tabs. */
const LABEL_FILE_LINE_RE = /^(\S+)[ \t]+(\S+)[ \t]*$/;

/** @typedef {{ id: string, qid: string, arm: string, store_id: string, outcome: 'judged'|'judge-failed',
 *    judge: 'uncertain'|'fabricated'|null }} HandcheckItem */
/** @typedef {{ share: number, mapSha256: string, judged: Array<{ store_id: string, sha256: string, dir: string }>,
 *    items: HandcheckItem[], sampled: string[], required: string[], stamps: string[] }} HandcheckPlan */

/** The hand-check plan over every node's judged file (W2-D81, Q2, Q18). Each file, by its 1-based position k: W2-5b1's
 *  kind, section quiz, this record's sha (a file made under a predecessor is refused, naming the remedy), this frozen
 *  list's, this judge map's, this record's judge (model, rubric id and rubric sha) and the judge's reply cap, one of the
 *  record's nodes and only once; its items each a judge id of the map, named once across every file, whose question is on
 *  that node, `judged` with one of HANDCHECK_LABELS or `judge-failed` with none. A node that holds frozen questions and
 *  passes no file is refused. Then the gate's handcheckSample over every item, the arm read from the map. Pure: every
 *  refusal is `input-invalid` (data, never a TypeError: D-6309's rule).
 *  @param {{ record: any, recordSha256: string, frozenSha256: string, entries: Array<{ qid: string, store_id: string }>,
 *    map: Array<{ id: string, qid: string, arm: string }>, mapSha256: string,
 *    judged: Array<{ path: string, sha256: string, value: any }> }} o
 *  @returns {HandcheckPlan} */
export function handcheckPlanOf({ record, recordSha256, frozenSha256, entries, map, mapSha256, judged }) {
  const nodes = new Set(record.nodes.map((n) => n.store_id));
  const storeOfQid = new Map(entries.map((e) => [e.qid, e.store_id]));
  const mapById = new Map(map.map((m) => [m.id, m]));
  const judge = [record.judge_model, record.rubric_id, RUBRIC_SHA256[record.rubric_id]];
  const seenStore = new Map();
  /** @type {Map<string, HandcheckItem>} */
  const items = new Map();
  const files = [];
  const stamps = new Set();
  judged.forEach((j, n) => {
    const k = n + 1;
    const d = j.value;
    const bad = (what) => refuse('input-invalid', `judged ${k} ${what}`);
    if (!plainObject(d) || d.kind !== JUDGED_KIND || d.v !== 1) bad('is not a judged file');
    if (d.section !== HANDCHECK_SECTION) bad(`section ${JSON.stringify(d.section ?? null)}, wanted ${HANDCHECK_SECTION}`);
    if (d.record_sha256 !== recordSha256) bad(`record ${JSON.stringify(d.record_sha256 ?? null)}, not this record's ${recordSha256}: run judge on that node under this record`);
    if (d.frozen_sha256 !== frozenSha256) bad(`frozen ${JSON.stringify(d.frozen_sha256 ?? null)}, not this record's ${frozenSha256}`);
    if (d.map_sha256 !== mapSha256) bad(`map ${JSON.stringify(d.map_sha256 ?? null)}, not this record's judge map ${mapSha256}`);
    if (!nodes.has(d.store_id)) bad(`store ${JSON.stringify(d.store_id ?? null)} is not one of the record's nodes`);
    if (seenStore.has(d.store_id)) bad(`store ${d.store_id} repeats judged ${seenStore.get(d.store_id)}`);
    seenStore.set(d.store_id, k);
    const theirs = [d.judge_model, d.rubric_id, d.rubric_sha256];
    if (theirs.some((v, i) => v !== judge[i])) bad(`judge ${JSON.stringify(theirs)} is not the record's ${JSON.stringify(judge)}`);
    if (d.reply_max_bytes !== JUDGE_REPLY_MAX_BYTES) bad(`reply_max_bytes ${JSON.stringify(d.reply_max_bytes ?? null)}, not ${JUDGE_REPLY_MAX_BYTES}`);
    if (!Array.isArray(d.stamps) || !d.stamps.every((s) => typeof s === 'string')) bad('stamps is not a list of words');
    if (!Array.isArray(d.items)) bad('items is not a list');
    for (const it of d.items) {
      if (!plainObject(it) || typeof it.id !== 'string' || !JUDGE_ID_RE.test(it.id)) bad(`item ${JSON.stringify(plainObject(it) ? it.id ?? null : null)} is not a judge id`);
      const m = mapById.get(it.id);
      if (m === undefined) bad(`item ${it.id} is not in the judge map`);
      if (items.has(it.id)) bad(`item ${it.id} repeats`);
      if (storeOfQid.get(m.qid) !== d.store_id) bad(`item ${it.id} names a question of another node`);
      if (it.outcome !== 'judged' && it.outcome !== 'judge-failed') bad(`item ${it.id} outcome ${JSON.stringify(it.outcome ?? null)}`);
      const labelled = it.outcome === 'judged' ? HANDCHECK_LABELS.includes(it.label) : it.label === null;
      if (!labelled) bad(`item ${it.id} ${it.outcome} with label ${JSON.stringify(it.label ?? null)}`);
      items.set(it.id, { id: it.id, qid: m.qid, arm: m.arm, store_id: d.store_id, outcome: it.outcome, judge: it.label });
    }
    for (const s of d.stamps) stamps.add(s);
    files.push({ store_id: d.store_id, sha256: j.sha256, dir: path.dirname(j.path) });
  });
  const missing = [...new Set(entries.map((e) => e.store_id))].filter((s) => !seenStore.has(s)).sort(cmpUnit);
  if (missing.length > 0) refuse('input-invalid', `judged-missing ${missing.length} node(s) (first ${missing[0]}): pass every node's judged.json that holds frozen questions`);
  const list = [...items.values()].sort((x, y) => cmpUnit(x.id, y.id));
  const pool = list.map((i) => ({ id: i.id, arm: i.arm, judged: i.outcome === 'judged', judgeFailed: i.outcome === 'judge-failed' }));
  const sampled = handcheckSample(record.bootstrap.seed, pool, record.handcheck.share);   // W2-D81: the gate's sampler at the signed share
  const judgedIds = new Set(list.filter((i) => i.outcome === 'judged').map((i) => i.id));
  return { share: record.handcheck.share, mapSha256, judged: files.sort((x, y) => cmpUnit(x.store_id, y.store_id)), items: list,
    sampled, required: sampled.filter((id) => judgedIds.has(id)), stamps: [...stamps].sort(cmpUnit) };
}

/** Q2: the plan over every `--judged` file, each read by its sha (loadInput), against the judge map recomputed from the
 *  record's seed and frozen list (W2-5b1 Task 5's judgeMapOf and judgeMapText: the bytes every node pinned). It writes
 *  nothing and takes no --out, so its caller runs it before prepareOut (W2-5a's R10). `fin` is loadFinalRecord's answer.
 *  @param {Flags} flags  @param {{ record: any, sha256: string, frozen: any, stamps: string[] }} fin  @returns {HandcheckPlan} */
export function loadHandcheckPlan(flags, fin) {
  const r = fin.record;
  const map = judgeMapOf(r.bootstrap.seed, fin.frozen.list.entries, RECALL_ARMS);
  const mapSha256 = sha256Hex(judgeMapText(HANDCHECK_SECTION, fin.frozen.sha256, map));
  const judged = pairedInputs(flags, 'judged').map(([p, h]) => loadInput('judged', p, h));
  return handcheckPlanOf({ record: r, recordSha256: fin.sha256, frozenSha256: fin.frozen.sha256, entries: fin.frozen.list.entries, map, mapSha256, judged });
}

/** A judge input file's fault, or null (W2-D79, D-6470): exactly W2-5b1's six keys, v 1, the four strings (the answer
 *  field a string or null), the frozen entry's kind, the reply and the answer field within JUDGE_REPLY_MAX_BYTES, and the
 *  bytes exactly canonicalJson of what they parse to and one newline (so an invalid UTF-8 byte is a fault). Pure.
 *  @param {unknown} v  @param {{ kind: string }} entry  @param {Buffer} bytes
 *  @returns {null | 'keys' | 'version' | 'field-type' | 'kind' | 'over-cap' | 'not-canonical'} */
export function judgeInputFault(v, entry, bytes) {
  if (!plainObject(v) || Object.keys(v).sort(cmpUnit).join(',') !== JUDGE_INPUT_KEYS.join(',')) return 'keys';
  if (v.v !== 1) return 'version';
  if (typeof v.question !== 'string' || typeof v.expected !== 'string' || typeof v.reply !== 'string'
    || (v.answer_field !== null && typeof v.answer_field !== 'string')) return 'field-type';
  if (v.kind !== entry.kind) return 'kind';
  const over = (s) => s !== null && Buffer.byteLength(s, 'utf8') > JUDGE_REPLY_MAX_BYTES;
  if (over(v.reply) || over(v.answer_field)) return 'over-cap';
  if (!Buffer.from(`${canonicalJson(v)}\n`, 'utf8').equals(bytes)) return 'not-canonical';
  return null;
}

/** One sampled item's judge input, as judge pinned it beside its node's judged.json (`judge/<id>.input.json`), read
 *  through readPlain (D-5986: a link or a FIFO is never followed or waited on) and held to judgeInputFault; every failure
 *  is `input-invalid`, naming the node and the path. */
function readJudgeInputFile(dir, storeId, id, entry) {
  const where = `judged ${storeId} ${JUDGE_DIR}/${id}.input.json`;
  const read = readPlain(path.join(dir, JUDGE_DIR, `${id}.input.json`), OUT_JSON_CAP);
  if (read.state === 'absent') refuse('input-invalid', `${where} unreadable ENOENT`);
  if (read.state === 'bad') refuse('input-invalid', `${where} ${badWord(read)}`);
  let v;
  try {
    v = JSON.parse(read.bytes.toString('utf8'));
  } catch {
    refuse('input-invalid', `${where} not-json`);
  }
  const why = judgeInputFault(v, entry, read.bytes);
  if (why !== null) refuse('input-invalid', `${where} ${why}`);
  return { input: v, sha256: sha256Hex(read.bytes) };
}

/** The sheet's text (W2-D81): a header naming the record and the frozen list, the item count, the labelling rule and the
 *  signed rubric the judge was given (as `#` lines), then one block per item in the order given: `== <id> ==`, its kind,
 *  and its question, F (`expected`), answer field and reply, each line of a field quoted `| ` (an empty line `|`), so no
 *  reply line can open a block. It takes an id and an input per item and nothing else: no arm, no judge label, no judge
 *  outcome reaches it. Pure.
 *  @param {{ recordSha256: string, frozenSha256: string, rubricId: string, items: Array<{ id: string, input: any }> }} o
 *  @returns {string} */
export function handcheckSheetText({ recordSha256, frozenSha256, rubricId, items }) {
  if (!RUBRIC_IDS.includes(rubricId)) throw new TypeError(`handcheckSheetText: rubric ${JSON.stringify(rubricId)} is not one of ${RUBRIC_IDS.join(', ')}`);
  const quote = (text) => text.split('\n').map((l) => (l === '' ? '|' : `| ${l}`));
  const lines = [
    '# ccrc history W2 hand-check sheet (W2-D81): one block per item, in id order.',
    `# record ${recordSha256}`,
    `# frozen ${frozenSha256}`,
    `# items ${items.length}`,
    '# Label every item in a separate file, one line per item: "<id> uncertain" or "<id> fabricated".',
    '# A line that starts with "#" is a comment. Neither the arm nor the judge\'s label is shown here.',
    `# The rubric the judge was given (${rubricId}):`,
    ...RUBRICS[rubricId].split('\n').map((l) => `#   ${l}`),
  ];
  for (const { id, input } of items) {
    lines.push('', `== ${id} ==`, `kind: ${input.kind}`, 'question:', ...quote(input.question), 'expected:', ...quote(input.expected),
      ...(input.answer_field === null ? ['answer field: (none)'] : ['answer field:', ...quote(input.answer_field)]),
      'reply:', ...quote(input.reply));
  }
  return `${lines.join('\n')}\n`;
}

/** The sheet and its manifest for a plan (W2-D81): each sampled item's input read from beside its node's judged file
 *  (readJudgeInputFile), the sheet over {id, input} alone, and the manifest naming the record, the frozen list, the map,
 *  the rubric, the share, each judged file by store and sha, each input by sha, the sheet by sha, and the stamps (the
 *  record's and every judged file's). Neither names an arm, a judge label or a judge outcome. It reads, never writes.
 *  @param {{ record: any, sha256: string, frozen: any, stamps: string[] }} fin  @param {HandcheckPlan} plan
 *  @returns {{ sheetText: string, manifestText: string }} */
export function handcheckSheetOf(fin, plan) {
  const entryOf = new Map(fin.frozen.list.entries.map((e) => [e.qid, e]));
  const dirOf = new Map(plan.judged.map((j) => [j.store_id, j.dir]));
  const byId = new Map(plan.items.map((i) => [i.id, i]));
  const read = plan.sampled.map((id) => {
    const it = byId.get(id);
    return { id, ...readJudgeInputFile(dirOf.get(it.store_id), it.store_id, id, entryOf.get(it.qid)) };
  });
  const sheetText = handcheckSheetText({ recordSha256: fin.sha256, frozenSha256: fin.frozen.sha256, rubricId: fin.record.rubric_id,
    items: read.map(({ id, input }) => ({ id, input })) });
  const manifestText = `${canonicalJson({
    kind: HANDCHECK_SHEET_KIND, v: 1, section: HANDCHECK_SECTION, record_sha256: fin.sha256, frozen_sha256: fin.frozen.sha256,
    map_sha256: plan.mapSha256, rubric_id: fin.record.rubric_id, share: plan.share,
    judged: plan.judged.map(({ store_id, sha256 }) => ({ store_id, sha256 })),
    items: read.map(({ id, sha256 }) => ({ id, input_sha256: sha256 })),
    sheet_sha256: sha256Hex(sheetText), stamps: [...new Set([...fin.stamps, ...plan.stamps])].sort(cmpUnit),
  })}\n`;
  return { sheetText, manifestText };
}

/** The operator's label file (Q19), against the plan's sheet: blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped;
 *  every other line is `<id>`, spaces or tabs, one of HANDCHECK_LABELS, and nothing after but spaces or tabs. An id must
 *  be on the sheet and given once; every sampled judged id (`required`) must be labelled. A judge-failed id may be left
 *  out: decideGate then holds the verdict at incomplete (W2-D81). Every refusal is `input-invalid`. Pure.
 *  @param {string} text  @param {HandcheckPlan} plan  @returns {Map<string, string>} */
export function parseHandcheckLabels(text, plan) {
  if (typeof text !== 'string') throw new TypeError('parseHandcheckLabels: text is a string');
  const sheet = new Set(plan.sampled);
  /** @type {Map<string, string>} */
  const labels = new Map();
  text.split('\n').forEach((line, i) => {
    const n = i + 1;
    if (/^[ \t]*$/.test(line) || line.startsWith('#')) return;
    const m = line.match(LABEL_FILE_LINE_RE);   // String#match, not the RegExp method: W2-4 Task 5's no-shell scan reds on a code line spelling exec
    if (m === null || !JUDGE_ID_RE.test(m[1])) refuse('input-invalid', `labels line ${n} is not "<id> ${HANDCHECK_LABELS.join('|')}"`);
    if (!HANDCHECK_LABELS.includes(m[2])) refuse('input-invalid', `labels line ${n} label ${JSON.stringify(m[2])} is not one of ${HANDCHECK_LABELS.join(', ')}`);
    if (!sheet.has(m[1])) refuse('input-invalid', `labels line ${n} id ${m[1]} is not on the sheet`);
    if (labels.has(m[1])) refuse('input-invalid', `labels line ${n} repeats ${m[1]}`);
    labels.set(m[1], m[2]);
  });
  const absent = plan.required.filter((id) => !labels.has(id));
  if (absent.length > 0) refuse('input-invalid', `labels-missing ${absent.length} sampled id(s) (first ${absent[0]}): label every sampled item`);
  return labels;
}

/** The label file by its sha, as every input is read (loadInputBytes: outside any git tree, the sha before a byte is
 *  decoded), decoded as strict UTF-8 (`labels not-utf8`), then parseHandcheckLabels. Task 5's report calls it.
 *  @param {string} p  @param {string} sha256  @param {HandcheckPlan} plan  @returns {Map<string, string>} */
export function readHandcheckLabels(p, sha256, plan) {
  const { bytes } = loadInputBytes('labels', p, sha256);
  let text;
  try {
    text = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(bytes);
  } catch {
    refuse('input-invalid', 'labels not-utf8');
  }
  return parseHandcheckLabels(text, plan);
}

/** W2-D81's effect, through the gate's two rules: the operator's label replaces the judge's on every item the operator
 *  labelled (applyHandcheck), every other judged item keeps the judge's, and a judge-failed item the operator left out
 *  keeps no label (decideGate's incomplete); agreement is handcheckAgreement over every sampled judged item (a judge-failed
 *  item has no judge label, so it is no pair), answered as the gate answers it, by arm. Pure. An operator id that is not
 *  on the sheet is a TypeError: parseHandcheckLabels never answers one.
 *  @param {HandcheckPlan} plan  @param {Map<string, string>} operator */
export function handcheckResultOf(plan, operator) {
  if (!(operator instanceof Map)) throw new TypeError('handcheckResultOf: the operator labels are a Map');
  const onSheet = new Set(plan.sampled);
  for (const id of operator.keys()) if (!onSheet.has(id)) throw new TypeError(`handcheckResultOf: ${id} is not on the sheet`);
  const byId = new Map(plan.items.map((i) => [i.id, i]));
  const judgeLabels = new Map(plan.items.filter((i) => i.outcome === 'judged').map((i) => [i.id, i.judge]));
  const labels = applyHandcheck(judgeLabels, operator);
  const pairs = plan.required.map((id) => ({ arm: byId.get(id).arm, judge: byId.get(id).judge, operator: operator.get(id) }));
  const agreement = handcheckAgreement(pairs);
  const items = plan.items.map((i) => {
    const failed = i.outcome === 'judge-failed';
    return { id: i.id, qid: i.qid, arm: i.arm, label: labels.get(i.id) ?? null, judgeFailed: failed, operator: operator.get(i.id) ?? null };
  });
  return { items, agreement, unlabelled: items.filter((i) => i.judgeFailed && i.label === null).map((i) => i.id) };
}

/** `handcheck --sheet` (W2 decisions §5 act 22; W2-D81; Q2): on the reporting node. In order: the form's flags; the part 2
 *  record through loadFinalRecord, which re-checks gate_code before any other input (W2-D24) and answers
 *  --allow-code-change as a stamp after window start only (Q23); every node's judged file and the plan; every sampled
 *  item's input and the two texts, all before --out exists (W2-5a's R10); then --out, its claim, and the sheet and its
 *  manifest pinned (pinOutBytes: a sheet the operator may be labelling never changes under them). Prints only
 *  `sha256 <hex>` of the manifest on stderr (D-5983).
 *  @param {Flags} flags  @param {DriverEnv} driverEnv
 *  @param {{ loadFinal: typeof loadFinalRecord, now: () => number }} [deps] */
export async function handcheckCommand(flags, driverEnv, deps = { loadFinal: loadFinalRecord, now: () => Date.now() }) {
  if (flags.sheet !== true) refuse('args-invalid', 'handcheck wants --sheet');
  checkFlags('handcheck --sheet', flags);
  const fin = deps.loadFinal(flags, { nowMs: deps.now() });   // W2-D24: gate_code before any other input
  const plan = loadHandcheckPlan(flags, fin);   // Q2: every node's judged file by its sha, held to this record and its map
  const sheet = handcheckSheetOf(fin, plan);   // every sampled item's input, read before --out exists (W2-5a's R10)
  const out = prepareOut(flags.out);
  const claim = claimOut(out);
  try {
    ensurePlainDir(out, HANDCHECK_DIR);
    const sheetRel = `${HANDCHECK_DIR}/${HANDCHECK_SHEET_FILE}`;
    pinOutBytes(out, sheetRel, sheet.sheetText, 'handcheck-sheet');
    const rel = `${HANDCHECK_DIR}/${HANDCHECK_MANIFEST_FILE}`;
    pinOutBytes(out, rel, sheet.manifestText, 'handcheck-manifest');
    process.stderr.write(`sha256 ${shaOfPlain(out, rel)}\n`);   // D-5983: stderr; stdout stays empty
    return EXIT.OK;
  } finally {
    claim.release();
  }
}

HANDLERS.set('handcheck', (flags, env) => handcheckCommand(flags, env));
```

### Task 5: `report --record <final>`: every node's gathered outputs, each sha-checked, into decideGate's inputs; verdict.json; the report-only figures (W2-D85, W2-D89, W2-D23, W2-D82, W2-D24; S2's C15 and C21, Q2, Q15, Q16, Q23, Q28, V1, K27)

This task ships W2's verdict act (decisions §5, act 24): one subcommand, `report`, run on the reporting node after window end over the files act 24 gathers there. It decides nothing. It checks every input, gathers `decideGate`'s inputs, calls `decideGate` once, and writes its answer whole into `--out/verdict.json`, printing that file's sha on stderr (W2-D85, W2-D89; D-5983):

- **The record first (W2-D24, W2-D25; Q23).** W2-5b1 Task 1's `loadFinalRecord` (re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged head) is the one part 2 loader. It takes the final with its chain (`--part1`, `--frozen`, and `--supersedes` for an amended final), then W2-D24's `gate_code` re-check before any other input is read, then the part 2 ranges (S2's C22). `--allow-code-change` is taken at or after `window.start_ms` only, and a measured change becomes the `code-changed` stamp on the verdict. `report` then refuses before `window.end_ms` (`window-open`; acts 23 and 24 come after window end).
- **Every input passed with its sha and sha-checked before a byte is parsed (Q2; W2-5a's `loadInput`).** From each quiz node (a store the frozen list holds questions on):
  - its arms summary, `quiz/arms/summary.json` inside that node's gathered `--out`. The answer records beside it are held to it (below);
  - its `quiz/judged.json` (W2-5b1 Task 5);
  - its `verify --section quiz` output (W2-5b1 Task 3), which carries D-6284's over-hide count (Q16);
  - its `quiz-source` output (W2-5a), which carries W2-D34's `asof_same_ms_hits`.

  From every named node: its `verify --section ab` output (Q15's `unrealised`) and its `measure-history.py --families` report. From the operator: the hand-check label file (W2-5b2 Task 4's reader; Q19). Each file is keyed by the `store_id` it names, one per store, and the store must be the record's.
- **Every input held to the record and to the others.**
  - The summaries, judged files and verify outputs name this record's sha. An answer record is written once, so it keeps the record that was in force when its question settled.
  - Every question is settled (W2-D80).
  - The answer records match the summary byte for byte through W2-5b1's own `armsSummaryOf`. This includes its `payload_changed` summary field: `nodeAnswersOf` derives sorted, deduplicated qids from the records, then supplies them back to `armsSummaryOf`; it never trusts that field as a second source.
  - K27 (W2-5b1's build departure; re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged code): a record whose `question_state` is `run-failed` and whose own optional `reason` equals `ARM_PAYLOAD_CHANGED` identifies a payload-drift exclusion. Its answered sibling also carries `question_state: 'run-failed'`, but has `arm_state: 'answered'` and no `reason`; the reader therefore scans every record, selects the reason-bearing record only, and deduplicates and sorts its qid. That question continues through the existing `run-failed` path into `decideGate`, including W2-D89's threshold; no new driver reason or answer-state vocabulary is introduced.
  - The judged items are exactly the non-correct answers of answered questions. The judge map's sha is recomputed from the record's seed over the frozen list (R18).
  - `assembleReports` checks the measure reports (W2-D22), and `changedFamilies` reads their presence rows (W2-D23).
- **decideGate's inputs (W2-D89).**
  - The quiz, keyed by `familyKey` (RP7). Each arm's label is `correct` from the string match, or the judge's label after the operator's override (`applyHandcheck`, W2-D81). A judge-failed answer the operator has not labelled has a null label, which is the hold.
  - The live families as `assembleReports` gives them, each marked `changed` (W2-D23) and `unrealised` when its verify state is not `ok` (V1).
  - The hand-check agreement by arm (`handcheckAgreement`).
  - The report-only figures, which `decideGate` echoes untouched.
- **The report-only figures** (W2-D85's list, Q15, Q16, S2's C15):
  - quiz counts and quiz uptake by arm, with `via_agent` (W2-D82), `unmeasured` (never 0) when the pilot found that the control arm's exit 8 is not `is_error`, and marked `aggregate-only` when V1 or W2-D23 drops a quiz family (K24);
  - live uptake per window and per turn, by arm and by producer;
  - the first-call difference, through the gate's `splitAtFirstExit8`, with the control calls after the first exit 8 reported apart;
  - the dropped families, each under its own word;
  - the presence gap rows and `assembleReports`' exclusions;
  - the judge's labels and the hand-check, by arm;
  - `asof_same_ms_hits`;
  - D-6284's over-hide count per node;
  - payload-drift exclusions: `{count, qids}`, derived from the reason-bearing `run-failed` answer records in deterministic qid order (K27; W2-5b1's build departure; re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged code). It is report-only, while those same questions remain in `quiz_counts` and W2-D89's `run_failed` count;
  - the read instant: each measure-history file's mtime as a labelled proxy, beside the report's own instant (S2's C15).

  V1 applies to every per-arm figure: a family whose verify state is `control-absent`, `control-mismatch`, `treatment-named` or `unreadable`, or which changed in the window (W2-D23), leaves every per-arm figure and is listed under its own word. These are the same families W2-6's counters drop.

Nothing here reads a HOME, opens a store or spawns a run, so every refusal answers before `prepareOut` makes `--out` (W2-5a's R10; D-6307), and no data case after `--out` exits INTERNAL (D-6309's rule). The driver never spells an arm word: every per-arm value is keyed by `RECALL_ARMS`' members at run time (W2-D42).

**Decisions:**
- W2-D85: the report checks the record with its amendments, `gate_code` and the frozen sha; reads the arm and judge outputs, the hand-check labels and every node's measure-history report; calls `decideGate`; writes `verdict.json` and prints its sha. Its report-only list, every amendment and the `code-changed` stamp included. The counters print beside it, never as inputs.
- W2-D89: `decideGate` is the gate's. The report gathers its inputs: Q, run-failed out of both arms, labels after the override, the live A/B over every listed treatment family with the changed and unrealised drops left to `decideGate`'s comparison block, and the agreement by arm.
- W2-D22: `assembleReports`, its refusals mapped to the driver's words.
- W2-D23, as V1 extends it: the changed and unrealised drops apply to the reported arm comparisons only. Criterion 3 is untouched, and its pin (a changed treatment family still counts in criterion 3) runs through the report.
- W2-D24, W2-D25, W2-D6, through `loadFinalRecord`; Q23 (`--allow-code-change` after window start only, the verdict stamped).
- W2-D80: run-failed questions are excluded from both arms; a summary with a question still owing a re-run or not run is refused. K27's `ARM_PAYLOAD_CHANGED` is one existing-record reason for that state (W2-5b1's build departure; re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged code), not a new state or a driver reason.
- W2-D81: the operator's labels replace the judge's on the sample; agreement by arm; the hold.
- W2-D82: quiz uptake by arm with `via_agent`, unmeasured when the pilot says so, and marked `aggregate-only` when a quiz family is dropped (K24).
- W2-D34: `asof_same_ms_hits` gathered.
- W2-D84: the verify outputs are read as data, every state apart.
- W2-D79 and W2-D18: the judge map is re-derived, never trusted (R18).
- W2-D12: the report's words are driver-local, and every list it uses is imported or derived.
- W2-D42: no arm word in the driver.
- W2-D53: `verdict.json` is written once.
- W2-D86 and W2-D88: W2-6's counters stay their own entry's.
- Rulings: S2's C15 (read instant) and C21 (report words); Q2, Q15, Q16, Q23, Q28; V1 (the state set) and U15 (line-disjoint from W2-6); R18 (map global across nodes) and R20 (settledness), both W2-5b1's, read here; and the coordinator's rulings K4 (Task 2's and Task 4's names, and Task 4's `judged` flags), K8 (node outputs name the current record), K11 (a stale presence record refused, as W2-6's V2), K12 (V1 reaches every per-arm figure, quiz uptake and the judge tallies by arm included, and not the hand-check sample), K23 (the walk's `verify --section ab` outputs built with `verifyAbReport`, its fixture stores holding no presence record: a fixture choice and a prediction, R32's rule), K24 (D-6646's residual stated as it is: the node summaries pin uptake and answer-field values only as per-arm sums, so quiz uptake by arm is marked `aggregate-only` when a quiz family is dropped), and K27: an `ARM_PAYLOAD_CHANGED` reason on exactly one run-failed arm record makes that question a report-only payload-drift exclusion while the existing W2-D89 run-failed count keeps it (W2-5b1's build departure; re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged code).

It cites D-5983 (the sha line), D-5986 (the plain I/O under `--out`), D-6307 and D-6309's rule (refusals before `--out`, a data case never INTERNAL), D-6284 (the over-hide count), D-5787 (decideGate's cluster order) and D-5770 (the window in Node), each bare. **Choices this task makes:**
- **The answer records are held to their summary, not passed one by one** (**D-6646**). Q2 and W2-D85 have the report read "each passed with its sha". An answer record is one file per (qid, arm) with no printed sha, and an operator cannot copy hundreds of shas by hand. So the record files are read from the node's gathered `--out`, located by the sha-checked arms summary, which must sit at that `--out`'s `quiz/arms/summary.json`. W2-5b1's own `armsSummaryOf`, run over them, must reproduce the summary's bytes, sha included. That pins, for each node, the per-arm sums the summary holds: answered; the answer-field states value, unknown and absent (the absent rate is a gate input); correct; and uptake (the questions with a call, `calls`, `via_agent` and `errored`). A question's uptake and its answer-field value are pinned only through those per-arm sums, never question by question (K24). The sha-checked judged file pins which answers are non-correct, question by question, because its items must be exactly those. Every gate input taken from an answer record therefore stays fixed by a sha-checked file. Two things are left free, and no gate input reads either: the order of non-correct answer states between questions of one arm; and how a node's per-arm uptake sums divide between its questions. The second reaches only the report-only quiz uptake by arm, and only when V1 or W2-D23 drops a quiz family. With no quiz family dropped, that figure sums every answered question, equals the summaries' sums and is exactly pinned. With one dropped, `quizUptakeOf` marks it `aggregate-only` (K24). Each record's own sha goes into `verdict.json`.
- **Node outputs name the current record (K8).** Summaries, judged files and both verify outputs must name this record's sha. After a mid-window amendment the operator re-runs, on each node, `arms --section quiz` and `judge --section quiz` (both resume and spawn nothing for settled work, W2-D53) and both `verify` sections. W2-6's V4 asks the same of its verify input. Answer records are exempt: each is written once, under the record in force when its question settled, and amendments only append (W2-D90).
- **Window end first.** `report` refuses before `window.end_ms` (`window-open`). The window is half-open, so at `end_ms` exactly it runs. A report before window end would assemble partial windows under the record's own echo.
- **One verdict, once.** `verdict.json` is never replaced (`out-refused`), as a frozen list is never replaced. The remedy is a fresh `--out`.
- **The per-arm report-only figures drop the same families W2-6 drops (V1).** That means every changed family and every family whose verify state is not `ok`, each listed apart under its own `REPORT_DROPS` word and never folded. Quiz uptake drops a question whose family carries such a state too ("every per-arm figure"), and its `by_arm` is then marked `aggregate-only`, because the node summaries pin uptake only as per-arm sums (K24). A quiz family that is not assigned has no verify state and stays. `decideGate`'s own inputs are not narrowed: criterion 3 reads every listed treatment family, and the gate's comparison block applies the drops (W2-D23).
- **The first-call difference** (spec §10.2: "treatment − control on the first-call indicator, counting control calls only up to the session's first exit 8"). A control family's calls are cut by the gate's `splitAtFirstExit8`; a treatment family's are not cut. The indicator is a measured window with at least one call. The difference is an exact fraction, null when either arm has no window. The control calls after the first exit 8 are counted apart.
- **How uptake reads W2-2b's carry.** An env call on a legacy family writes no `gen` on its counter line, so the drain files the row under the registry's current generation. Two facts keep that row out of both of this report's uptake figures:
  - Live uptake reads only `measure-history.py`'s `calls`, which are `recall_calls` rows with `arm IS NULL`. A replay arm's row always carries its arm, whatever generation it was filed under, so it never reaches a live window.
  - Quiz uptake reads only each arm run's own stream facts, carried on its answer record (W2-D82). It reads no `recall_calls` row and no counter.

  A scan pins that the report's code names neither `recall_calls` nor `.counters`.
- **W2-6's counters stay apart.** W2-6 ships its own entry, `deploy/history-counters.mjs`, and its own `counters.json` (W2-D88). The driver never imports it, `report` takes no counters input (no such flag exists), `decideGate` never sees a counter, and `verdict.json` names none. The operator runs both after window end (act 23), and the counters print beside the verdict (W2-D85). A scan pins that the report's section never names the counter's file or output.
- **The report decides nothing.** Exactly one code line in the driver calls `decideGate(`, and its answer goes into `verdict.json` unchanged. No code line of the section spells a verdict word.
- **Families are keyed by `familyKey`.** Both the quiz clusters (`familyKeyOf`, W2-5a's, over the gate's `familyKey`) and the live families (`assembleReports`' keys). `verdict.json` carries the keys `decideGate` was given, so RP7 is read through the report.
- **The read instant** is the measure file's mtime. A copy that does not keep mtimes moves it later. It is labelled a proxy, and a `.py` read-instant field stays a W2-3 follow-up (S2's C15).

**Residuals, named:** the answer records' non-correct states can be permuted between questions of one arm without a red, because no gate input reads that order. A node's per-arm uptake sums can be moved between its questions without a red (K24): every gate input stays pinned, and the report-only quiz uptake by arm is exactly pinned only when V1 drops no quiz family; when one is dropped it is marked `aggregate-only`. K27's qid list exposes only the existing W2-5b1 payload-drift exclusion reason; it does not identify an arm beyond what the gathered answer records already disclose and does not distinguish an otherwise ordinary run-failed question in any gate input. The read instant is a proxy. `authentication_failed` is still unmeasured (W2-5b1's Q31 residual). The judge's and the sheet's reply text can reveal the arm (decisions §7), and agreement is reported by arm.

```ts
import { describe as b2t5Describe, expect as b2t5Expect, it as b2t5It, vi as b2t5Vi } from 'vitest';
import { utimesSync as b2t5Utimes } from 'node:fs';
import * as b2t5Drv from '../../deploy/history-replay.mjs';

import * as b2t5Lib from '../../ccd/history/lib.mjs';
import { mkTmp as b2t5MkTmp } from './tmpHelpers.js';

type B2t5R = Record<string, any>;
type B2t5Saved = { path: string; sha: string; value: any };
type B2t5Result = { code: unknown; stdout: string; stderr: string; refusal: { word: string; detail: string } | null };
type B2t5Call = { command: string; isError?: boolean; parent?: string };
type B2t5Opts = {
  twin?: boolean;
  soloQuiz?: boolean;
  answer?: (e: B2t5R, arm: string) => { text: string; calls?: B2t5Call[] };
  runFailed?: (e: B2t5R) => boolean;
  /** K27 fixture: the control arm is the excluded owed arm; its answered sibling remains answer-bearing. */
  payloadChanged?: (e: B2t5R) => boolean;
  judgeLabel?: (qid: string, arm: string) => 'uncertain' | 'fabricated' | null;
  operator?: (id: string, judge: string | null) => string | null;
  ab?: (f: B2t5R) => string;
  liveCalls?: (f: B2t5R, w: number, ts: number) => Array<[number, number, string]>;
  recallOff?: Array<[string, string]>;
  hits?: (qid: string) => number;
  summaryStamps?: string[];
};
const B2T5 = b2t5Drv as unknown as B2t5R;
const B2T5_S1 = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000052a1';
const B2T5_S2 = '00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000052b1';
const B2T5_STORES = [B2T5_S1, B2T5_S2];
/** The arm values in W2-2b's frozen order, by position. */
const B2T5_ARMS: string[] = [...(b2t5Lib.RECALL_ARMS as readonly string[])];
const B2T5_C = B2T5_ARMS[0]!;
const B2T5_T = B2T5_ARMS[1]!;
const B2T5_START = W5B4_T0 + W5B4_DAY;
const B2T5_END = W5B4_T0 + 15 * W5B4_DAY;
/** After window end: report's clock (acts 23 and 24). */
const B2T5_NOW = W5B4_T0 + 16 * W5B4_DAY;
const b2t5Hex = (label: string): string => b2t5Lib.sha256Hex(`w2-5b2 task 5 fixture: ${label}`) as string;
const b2t5Key = (f: B2t5R): string => b2t5Gate.familyKey(f.store_id, f.ccrc_id, f.generation) as string;
/** The first generation of `id` on `store` whose arm under W5B4_SEED is `arm` (W2-D19), searched from n0. */
function b2t5Pick(store: string, id: string, arm: string, n0: number): W5b4Ref {
  for (let n = n0; ; n += 1) {
    const f = { store_id: store, ccrc_id: id, generation: w5b4Gen(n) };
    if (b2t5Gate.armOf(W5B4_SEED, f) === arm) return f;
  }
}
/** Text saved as the operator saves an output: 0600, in a fresh directory outside any git tree, with its bytes' sha. */
function b2t5SaveText(text: string, name: string): B2t5Saved {
  const p = join(b2t5MkTmp('ccrc-w5b2-t5-in-'), name);
  writeFileSync(p, text, { mode: 0o600 });

}
/** A saved JSON file rewritten in place with `value` (canonical JSON and one newline), and its new sha. */
function b2t5Rewrite(s: B2t5Saved, value: B2t5R): B2t5Saved {
  const text = `${b2t5Lib.canonicalJson(value) as string}\n`;

}
/** One answered (qid, arm)'s record, in W2-5b1 Task 4's answer-record fields, its answer by the driver's armAnswerOf. */
function b2t5Answered(recordSha: string, e: B2t5R, arm: string, a: { text: string; calls?: B2t5Call[] }, questionState: string): B2t5R {
  const toolPairs = (a.calls ?? []).map((c, i) => ({ id: `toolu_b2t5_${i}`, name: 'Bash', input: { command: c.command },
    result: c.isError === true ? 'exit 8' : 'ok', isError: c.isError === true, parentToolUseId: c.parent ?? null }));
  const ans = B2T5.armAnswerOf(e, { result: { text: a.text }, toolPairs }, 7) as B2t5R;
  const run = `quiz/arms/${e.qid as string}/${arm}.a1`;
  return { kind: B2T5.ANSWER_KIND, v: 1, section: 'quiz', record_sha256: recordSha, store_id: e.store_id, qid: e.qid, arm, ccrc_id: e.ccrc_id,
    generation: e.generation, boundary_uuid: e.boundary_uuid, fact_kind: e.kind, question_state: questionState, arm_state: 'answered',
    attempts: [{ name: run, class: 'answered', code: 0, signal: null, tokens: 65, error_fields: [] }], run, ...ans, stamps: [] };

/** A run-failed arm's record: two infrastructure failures and no answered attempt (W2-D80). */
function b2t5Failed(recordSha: string, e: B2t5R, arm: string): B2t5R {
  const names = [1, 2].map((n) => `quiz/arms/${e.qid as string}/${arm}.a${n}`);
  return { kind: B2T5.ANSWER_KIND, v: 1, section: 'quiz', record_sha256: recordSha, store_id: e.store_id, qid: e.qid, arm, ccrc_id: e.ccrc_id,
    generation: e.generation, boundary_uuid: e.boundary_uuid, fact_kind: e.kind, question_state: 'run-failed', arm_state: 'run-failed',
    attempts: names.map((name) => ({ name, class: 'infra-failed', code: 1, signal: null, tokens: 0, error_fields: [] })),
    run: null, answer_field: null, correct: null, absent: null, reply: null, uptake: null, stamps: [] };
}
/** K27's actual W2-5b1 departure shape: only the owed arm has the reason; its answered sibling retains its answer but shares
 * question_state run-failed, so the report must select the reason-bearing record and deduplicate qids rather than count states.
 * (W2-5b1's build departure; re-anchor at W2-5b1's merged code.) */
function b2t5PayloadChanged(recordSha: string, e: B2t5R, arm: string, a: { text: string; calls?: B2t5Call[] }): B2t5R {
  if (arm !== B2T5_C) return b2t5Answered(recordSha, e, arm, a, 'run-failed');
  return { ...b2t5Failed(recordSha, e, arm), reason: B2T5.ARM_PAYLOAD_CHANGED };

/** measure-history.py's --families report for one listed family, in its documented shape: one boundary per window inside the
 *  window, one copy each holding no assistant row and ending 1 s after it, so each window is measured with an inclusive end.
 *  A treatment family has three windows, each with one call; a control family two, the first with one call. */
function b2t5Family(a: B2t5R, i: number, o: B2t5Opts): B2t5R {
  const n = a.arm === B2T5_T ? 3 : 2;
  const calls: Array<[number, number, string]> = [];
  const boundaries = Array.from({ length: n }, (_, w) => {
    const ts = B2T5_START + 3_600_000 + i * 1_000_000 + w * 10_000;
    calls.push(...(o.liveCalls !== undefined ? o.liveCalls(a, w, ts) : a.arm === B2T5_T || w === 0 ? [[ts + 10, 0, 'grep'] as [number, number, string]] : []));
    return { boundary_uuid: w5b4Gen(7600 + i * 10 + w), ts_ms: ts, copies: [{ file_id: 1, source_key: '', boundary_line: 1 + w * 10, after_count: 1,
      summary_line: null, next_boundary_line: null, next_boundary_ts_ms: null, last_ts_ms: ts + 1000, rows: [], models: [], truncated: false }] };
  });
  return { ccrc_id: a.ccrc_id, generation: a.generation, found: true, merged_generations: [], calls, boundaries };
}

/** `report` in-process, as main runs it (parseArgs, then the handler): its clock after window end, the checkout as its code
 *  root and the pilot's uptake reading measured, unless `deps` says otherwise; stdout and stderr captured, a refusal
 *  answered as {word, detail}; any other throw is the case's failure (D-6309's rule). */
async function b2t5Report(argv: string[], deps: B2t5R = {}): Promise<B2t5Result> {
  const err: string[] = [];
  const out: string[] = [];
  const e1 = b2t5Vi.spyOn(process.stderr, 'write').mockImplementation(((s: string | Uint8Array) => { err.push(String(s)); return true; }) as typeof process.stderr.write);
  const o1 = b2t5Vi.spyOn(process.stdout, 'write').mockImplementation(((s: string | Uint8Array) => { out.push(String(s)); return true; }) as typeof process.stdout.write);
  try {
    const { flags } = B2T5.parseArgs(argv) as { flags: B2t5R };
    const code = await B2T5.reportCommand(flags, { HOME: undefined, TMUX_PANE: undefined, LANG: undefined },
      { now: () => B2T5_NOW, root: W5B4_REPO, uptakeReading: () => 'measured', ...deps });
    return { code, stdout: out.join(''), stderr: err.join(''), refusal: null };
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof b2t5Drv.DriverRefusal) return { code: null, stdout: out.join(''), stderr: err.join(''), refusal: { word: (e as B2t5R).word, detail: (e as B2t5R).detail } };
    throw e;
  } finally {
    e1.mockRestore();
    o1.mockRestore();
  }
}
```
